examples: Set the development root new projects are created under.
Type "port" in the search to jump straight to the bind address.
Change the default shell and the environment together, then save both at once from the bar at the bottom.
On a phone the page is one bar: the back arrow at the left, the title over the search in one frame, the filters that fit and one grid/list flip at the right.
Advanced, diagnostics: pick debug to see every detail in the server log while you troubleshoot, then back to info, with no restart.
how_to: Open settings; pick a section in the rail: account, appearance, sessions & agents, launch profiles, terminal, notifications, ai, pipeline, remote & security, general, keyboard shortcuts or advanced. On a phone the rail is a section picker beside the search.

A section with several groups is a tabbed page: sessions & agents has AUTO-SLEEP, AGENTS, TIME MACHINE and CONVERSATION INDEX tabs, appearance has COLORS, AGENT ROWS, STATUS BAR and CONTROL CENTER. Only the open tab's rows show.

Link straight to a tab with #settings/<section>/<tab>, for example #settings/sessions/agents. Plugin settings sit under the plugins heading at the bottom of the rail: one entry per plugin that is on and has settings (#settings/plugin/<id>), the same form as its pane on the plugins page, which the gear on its card also opens. The search finds them by field name, hint or plugin name.
Launch profiles and keyboard shortcuts are sections too: each opens its own screen inside settings.
Or type in the search box at the top of the rail to find a setting by name or what it does, and press enter to jump to its tab.
Each tab is one framed list: the label and its help on the left, the control on the right. A setting that depends on another sits indented under it and is greyed out while the other is off.

Switches and pickers apply at once and show saved. Typed values wait: a tab that holds one ends its frame with save changes and discard, dimmed until you type; a dot marks any tab and its rail item that holds an unsaved change.

Advanced, diagnostics: pick the server log level (error, warn, info or debug). It changes at once with no restart and is kept across restarts; the use LOG_LEVEL from .env button hands the choice back to the .env value (error on a new install, info when .env names none).
